initialUserIntent: Complete the Java project model part of JetBrains-style IDE management: present the Java project structure in the IDE by consuming RefactorKit's project-model surface (scan + symbols commands in real_engine.rs run_engine_scan/run_engine_symbols + workspace_registry workspace_id_for_path), NOT a standalone project-model kit. Prior user decision (obs 2026-07-11): the Java project model remains an internal, modular RefactorKit component and is extracted later only if independent external consumers and a stable reusable contract emerge. The IDE consumes the RefactorKit project model: given a workspace root, present packages/classes/symbols from the engine symbols scan, with honest-unavailable when the engine is absent.

approvedChanges.statement: Pi is, in the future, ONE of the usable agents in the IDE, not the sole AI/model authority.
User authorized RefactorKit as a PRODUCT FEATURE. Java TEST infra (JavaSpec/Maven/JUnit/dataset) and Java-only RefactorKit rules as workflow refactoring authority remain EXCLUDED.

No standalone Java Project Model Kit. Project-model capabilities remain internal, modular RefactorKit components, extracted later only if independent external consumers and a stable reusable contract emerge.

requirement.title: Java project model presented in the IDE by consuming RefactorKit
requirement.classification: Story BDD + Spec BDD for pure view-model decisions
requirement.capability: Present the Java project structure in the IDE by consuming RefactorKit's project-model surface (scan + symbols commands, workspace registry). Given a workspace root, the IDE requests the engine symbols scan and presents packages/classes/symbols as the project model, with honest-unavailable when the engine is absent or the scan fails. Follows the prior decision: the project model stays inside RefactorKit (no standalone kit); the IDE is a consumer.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a Java workspace root, the IDE requests the RefactorKit engine symbols scan and presents the project model (packages/classes/symbols) from the engine result.
Given the engine is absent or the scan fails, the IDE reports honest unavailable/error and never fabricates a project model.
The flow follows extract -> delegate -> response with no hidden domain policy; the project model comes from RefactorKit (no standalone kit, no reimplementation of the model).
Boundary invariant: packages/ui, packages/web-core, apps/web never import @tauri-apps/api; browser/Tauri project-model implementations live behind frontend ports.
Status is evidence-based with an explicit state, never inferred from shells; live Tauri-window project-model E2E may remain unvalidated if headless (recorded honestly).

requirement.owner: bdd-ts-domain-expert (domain research) + bdd-ts-gherkin-writer (feature) + ts-story-driven (Story) + tauri-rust-coder (engine scan/symbols) + tauri-adapter-coder + browser-adapter-coder + frontend-core-coder/frontend-app-coder (view-model + controller wiring)
requirement.scope: Java project model presented in the IDE by consuming RefactorKit scan + symbols (engine + workspace registry). The existing Java language service, navigation, refactoring, engine-integration slices stay as-is. Java build/run/debug and packaging remain separate later slices.
exclusions: JavaSpec, Maven, JUnit-specific policy, Java datasets as workflow test infra
Java-only RefactorKit rules as the workflow's own refactoring authority
Standalone Java Project Model Kit (prior decision: stays inside RefactorKit)
openQuestions: Source: whether the project model comes from the engine symbols scan (run_engine_symbols) or a richer scan (run_engine_scan) — confirm the primary source.
Editor wiring: whether project-model presentation is proven wired into a live panel or a desktop-harness renderer is acceptable evidence.
Reuse: whether to reuse the existing useRefactorKitSymbolNavigationController or add a Java project-model controller.
Scope: whether project-model presentation includes navigation (click a class -> open) or is read-only structure listing.
